title: A Nested Krylov Method Using Half-Precision Arithmetic
problem: Leveraging half-precision (fp16) arithmetic in iterative sparse linear solvers is challenging despite the bandwidth and performance benefits it offers.
motivation: Half-precision arithmetic enables significant bandwidth and compute efficiency gains, but low-precision solvers suffer convergence issues; mixed-precision strategies remain underdeveloped for fp16.
method: The method combines two iterative algorithms—FGMRES and Richardson—in a nested structure where the outer solver repeatedly uses the inner solver as part of its calculations. It starts with high-precision (64-bit) arithmetic and progressively reduces to half-precision (16-bit) arithmetic as it goes deeper into the nesting, gaining speed and reducing memory use. The inner solver runs for only a limited number of iterations each time—just enough to improve the solution without the rounding errors that normally break low-precision calculations. Since the inner solver repeats many times within the outer solver's work, these small improvements compound, and the nested feedback ensures the overall answer converges correctly.
key_novelty: This is the first nested solver to effectively use half-precision arithmetic—it keeps the low-precision inner solver's iterations deliberately limited so they don't accumulate rounding errors, while the nested repetition ensures the overall solution still converges correctly.
contributions: Nested Krylov-Richardson framework with progressive precision reduction
Up to 2.47x speedup over conventional mixed-precision CG
Direct fp16 integration without compromising convergence
limitations: Abstract-only; unclear on problem condition numbers, memory usage breakdown, or applicability to non-convex/non-symmetric systems
